entries.originalText: “My Son, he who striveth to withdraw himself from obedience, withdraweth himself also from grace, and he who seeketh private advantages, loseth those which are common unto all.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, he who strives to withdraw himself from obedience withdraws himself also from grace, and he who seeks private advantages loses those which are common to all.

entries.originalText: If a man submit not freely and willingly to one set over him, it is a sign that his flesh is not yet perfectly subject to himself, but often resisteth and murmureth.
entries.modernizedText: If a man does not submit freely and willingly to one set over him, it is a sign that his flesh is not yet perfectly subject to himself, but often resists and murmurs.

entries.originalText: Learn therefore quickly to submit thyself to him who is over thee, if thou seekest to bring thine own flesh into subjection.
entries.modernizedText: Learn therefore quickly to submit yourself to him who is over you, if you seek to bring your own flesh into subjection.

entries.originalText: For the outward enemy is very quickly overcome if the inner man have not been laid low.
entries.modernizedText: For the outward enemy is very quickly overcome if the inner man has not been laid low.

entries.originalText: There is no more grievous and deadly enemy to the soul than thou art to thyself, if thou art not led by the Spirit.
entries.modernizedText: There is no more grievous and deadly enemy to the soul than you are to yourself, if you are not led by the Spirit.

entries.originalText: Thou must not altogether conceive contempt for thyself, if thou wilt prevail against flesh and blood.
entries.modernizedText: You must not altogether conceive contempt for yourself, if you would prevail against flesh and blood.

entries.originalText: Because as yet thou inordinately lovest thyself, therefore thou shrinkest from yielding thyself to the will of others.
entries.modernizedText: Because you still love yourself inordinately, you shrink from yielding yourself to the will of others.

entries.originalText: “But what great thing is it that thou, who art dust and nothingness, yieldest thyself to man for God’s sake, when I, the Almighty and the Most High, who created all things out of nothing, subjected Myself to man for thy sake?
entries.modernizedText: “But what great thing is it that you, who are dust and nothingness, yield yourself to man for God’s sake, when I, the Almighty and the Most High, who created all things out of nothing, subjected Myself to man for your sake?

entries.originalText: I became the most humble and despised of men, that by My humility thou mightest overcome thy pride.
entries.modernizedText: I became the most humble and despised of men, that by My humility you might overcome your pride.

entries.originalText: Learn to humble thyself, O earth and clay, and to bow thyself beneath the feet of all.
entries.modernizedText: Learn to humble yourself, O earth and clay, and to bow yourself beneath the feet of all.

entries.originalText: Learn to crush thy passions, and to yield thyself in all subjection.
entries.modernizedText: Learn to crush your passions, and to yield yourself in all subjection.

entries.originalText: “Be zealous against thyself, nor suffer pride to live within thee, but so show thyself subject and of no reputation, that all may be able to walk over thee, and tread thee down as the clay in the streets.
entries.modernizedText: “Be zealous against yourself, and do not allow pride to live within you, but so show yourself subject and of no reputation, that all may be able to walk over you and tread you down like the clay in the streets.

entries.originalText: What hast thou, O foolish man, of which to complain?
entries.modernizedText: What have you, O foolish man, to complain of?

entries.originalText: What, O vile sinner, canst thou answer those who speak against thee, seeing thou hast so often offended God, and many a time hast deserved hell?
entries.modernizedText: What, O vile sinner, can you answer those who speak against you, seeing you have so often offended God, and many a time have deserved hell?

entries.originalText: But Mine eye hath spared thee, because thy soul was precious in My sight; that thou mightest know My love, and mightest be thankful for My benefits; and that thou mightest give thyself altogether to true subjection and humility, and patiently bear the contempt which thou meritest.”
entries.modernizedText: But My eye has spared you, because your soul was precious in My sight; that you might know My love, and might be thankful for My benefits; and that you might give yourself altogether to true subjection and humility, and patiently bear the contempt which you merit.”
